name: product-page
title: Product page
description: A page for one thing you make or launch, set like a newspaper front: a masthead with a dateline, the headline beside your picture, a row of key figures, then the story, a few promises as columns, and inner pages.

images.purpose: beside the headline on the home page; without it the headline runs alone
images.alt_hint: what the picture shows, e.g. An engraved bird at its nest
images.prompt: {subject} at work, doing what the product does, with one or two small details in the spot colour; square; subject in the lower two thirds, paper above

images.purpose: the mark beside the name in the masthead (46 px) and the browser icon; must still read at 32 px
images.prompt: the head of {subject} in profile, bold simple lines, little hatching, filling the frame; the spot colour on one small detail (an eye, a tip)

images.purpose: a small round photo of the owner in the masthead's follow link (shown alone on a phone); without it the link is words only
images.alt_hint: the owner's name, e.g. Sam Lee
images.prompt: a friendly head-and-shoulders photo of the owner, face centred, plain background; square

images.purpose: the picture when a link is shared on X or in messages; put the site name and headline in it, in the site's serif
images.alt_hint: the site name and headline, then what the picture shows
images.prompt: made from the hero: hero on the left, paper on the right for the site's name and headline

images.purpose: a wide band inside the front-page story: put ![description](image) on its own line between two sections
images.prompt: a wide scene from {subject}'s world without {subject} in it, a few small details in the spot colour, paper at both ends

images.purpose: spot art on an inner page, shown small (about 200 px) beside the words
images.prompt: one small object from {subject}'s world, alone, small in the frame, in the spot colour with black hatching

content.purpose: the dateline under the masthead, e.g. Vol. I — October 2026 · what it is · what it costs · its licence
the main button under the headline (with cta_link); cta2_label and cta2_link make a second
the menu in the masthead: usually the inner pages

one stream with layout feature: its newest entry is the front-page story (its stats are the row of figures, up to 4; its body is the story; a > quote is the pull quote). One stream with layout list: the inner pages (How it works, Install, ...)
cards print as columns under this heading: short promises or features
the footer line, e.g. the product's name and licence
an X handle: the masthead's follow link

art.ask: Pick one subject that stands for what your person makes (an animal or an object), with them. It appears in every picture, drawn the same way. Example: a site-building product uses a bowerbird, the bird that builds a display and keeps it.
art.style: Engraved illustration, like a 19th-century print: black ink linework and cross-hatching on plain off-white paper (not transparent), generous empty paper around the subject. One spot colour only (the site's accent, e.g. cyan #0088b0), used on one or two small details; everything else black ink. No words in any picture except the share picture.
art.prompt_prefix: 19th-century steel engraving, fine black ink linework with cross-hatching and stipple, on plain off-white paper, generous empty margins, no background scenery, no text, no frame.
steps: Agree the subject and the one spot colour with your person.
Make each picture in `images` from its prompt (replace {subject}; start every prompt with prompt_prefix), at its size. The subject must look the same in every picture.
Check each one: the right size and shape; an off-white ground, not transparent; the same paper colour edge to edge; only the one spot colour; no words except in the share picture.
Shrink the mark to 32 px. If it no longer reads as the subject, make it bolder and simpler and try again.
Make the share picture from the hero: the hero on the left, the site's name and headline on the right in a serif, nothing within 50 px of the edges.
Name each file by its slot, keep its alt text with it, and show your person the whole set before you use any of it.
Upload each one (an https link in its field, or photo_upload_link), then call theme_needs: every slot should say filled.
